meta.title: PaperPrinter endgame: what makes the work list grow or shrink in one round
meta.status: v1, 2026-11-20, claude-10: claude-1's fidelity check applied (~/notes/claude-1/paperprinter-endgame-model-check-2026-11-20.md); claude-7's check of the ledger pending
meta.scope: One round = one pass from a census to the next census on claude7/integrate (mfuton-share). The model is about the queue of packets, not about the printer's rules; rule conflicts are the subject of the 2026-11-17 DiagramProver work and enter here as one variable (rule_overlap).
meta.reading: Authored qualitative causal graph. An arrow says: changing the source can change the target, holding the target's other parents fixed. No effect sizes. Arrow status: definition (true by how the process is run), measured (an entry in claude-7's queue logs shows it), hypothesis (proposed, not observed).

assumptions: The loop census -> packets -> merge -> census is cut at the round boundary: defects_before is the state entering the round, defects_after the state leaving it. The graph is acyclic for that reason and says nothing about how many rounds there are.

freeze_list is not a variable. Freezing is the intervention do(admitted_classes): the classes that may enter the queue are set from a list written at one commit, which removes the arrow visible_classes -> admitted_classes.

corpus_scope and scanner_families are treated as choices made each round. Under a freeze they are held at one value; the graph cannot express 'held fixed', so that requirement is stated in check K5 and enforced by endgame.py, not by the graph.
One node stands for all packets of a round. Retries of one item (Q132 to Q132e) are counted in the ledger, not drawn.

arrows.mechanism: Packets are written for admitted classes.
A cap stops further packets on a class. Applied once by hand (Q116s: 'Third failure: STOPPED dispatching'); not applied to Q132 (five rounds).
A size floor keeps one-record classes out of the printer queue. Not applied today: Q105, Q107, Q112, Q126, Q127 changed one record each.
Only dispatched packets can be merged.
Review rejects packets.
arrows.evidence: ~/notes/claude-7/raw-names-480/proofs/r8/overnight/QUEUE.md: Q110, Q116, Q116r, Q116s, Q132, Q132c, Q132d, Q133 rejected

arrows.mechanism: A merged packet removes sites of its class.
Sites not touched stay.
A merge can change records it was not aimed at.
arrows.evidence: Q/QUEUE.md: Q56 truncated a97J08; Q97 added 13 'x = x' rows (caught in review); Q86b r2 changed 72 records against a target of about 10

arrows.mechanism: Regressions come where the edited rule overlaps another.
Review catches regressions before merge.
arrows.evidence: Q97 review fix; Q79c not merged (a97J06 regressed)

arrows.mechanism: Introduced sites are present afterwards.
The census counts the sites that are there.
The census counts only the records it renders.
The census counts only the patterns it knows.
A class leaves by a merged fix, or by the cap or the size floor sending it to a notation change or a residual.
Reaching the cap is an exit.
Being under the floor is an exit.
The end is: every admitted class has left.
The end is relative to the admitted list.
A class leaves as fixed only when its census count is zero. Not how it is done today: 'done' in classes.tsv is typed by hand from the queue log. Needs counts.tsv.
A merged fix, or a rejection that brings the class to the cap, is what makes a class leave.
Packets that edit a rule overlapping another are the ones rejected repeatedly, so overlap reaches the exits through the cap.
arrows.evidence: claude-1, ~/notes/claude-1/paperprinter-endgame-model-check-2026-11-20.md section 2; Q116 x3 and Q132 x3 are the candidates, pair check not run

checks.claim: As run today, a discovery packet can move the end: it adds classes, and every admitted class must leave before the end.
With the admitted list frozen, discovery packets cannot move the end.
With the admitted list frozen, rendering more records adds no packets.
With the admitted list frozen, a new census pattern adds no packets.

Freezing the list is not enough for the count to be comparable between rounds: the count still depends on which records are rendered. The corpus and the scanner have to be held at the freeze commit's values as well.
Rule overlap still reaches the count through regressions under a freeze, so the 2026-11-17 conflict checks stay in use.

Given which packets were dispatched and merged, a regression still moves the end, because the count decides exits (arrow measured_open -> exits_taken). Without that arrow this check fails. What stays open is O1: a regression of a kind no frozen pattern counts.
The cap and the size floor are the two settings that move the end once the list is frozen.

Rule overlap can move the end under a freeze, through rejections and the cap. So a class at the cap gets the critical-pair check before it is put to Joe as an exception: a conflict wants a guard or an order, not a residual.

open_questions.text: Regressions of a kind no frozen pattern counts. claude-1: 'records changed outside the target' is enough if (1) it is a byte comparison of rendered output, not of scanner hits, (2) it runs over the whole frozen corpus at every merge (or a fixed hashed sample taken at the freeze commit), (3) the number of changed records to be read has a bound above which the merge is rejected. Which of these claude-7's census-changed number meets is not known. A regression seen in review cannot become a new class under a freeze: reject the merge, or read and accept each change.
Values of attempt_cap and min_size. The dry run uses 3 and 2.
Does a class sent to 'Lean notation change' count as left when the change is planned or when the re-rendered record is clean?
Speed work (Q125, Q131, Q136, Q137) changes which proofs finish and so changes corpus_scope. Under a freeze it belongs before the freeze commit or after the end, not during.
'The best available packet opens more than it closes' is not computed: queue.tsv would need, per merged packet, sites closed in its class and sites opened anywhere.

The held-out 1,886 records were rendered in Q109 and read by discovery packets (Q120, Q121). If rules were written from them they are no longer held out; the end-of-run comparison then needs a fresh set nobody reads until the end.
Classes seen after the freeze and not admitted need their own ledger with a count, so that 'every failing evaluation classed' holds beyond the frozen list.
The cap is a budget of rejections, not a finding that no rendering exists. Every 'exception' from endgame.py is a proposal to Joe; none is a residual until he accepts it.
